notes:
Summary: ASA runs classified archival and operational analytic workloads; cannot have any outbound telemetry or cloud egress from production. They asked specifically for a fully air‑gapped Private offering deployable into a SCIF with HSM integration and STIG hardening. POC acceptance criteria: 1) run chat assistant on sealed model image without network, 2) embeddings generation on local batch nodes at 500 qps sustained for offline jobs, 3) integration with on‑prem KMS (FIPS 140‑2) for key material, 4) ability to do model updates via removable media with integrity verification.

Key quotes: "We will not allow telemetry or model callbacks to leave the facility — no compromise." — SecOps lead. "We need an ATO path and STIG checklist to our RMF control set before procurement." — ISSO.

Technical notes: Customer prefers open‑license models we can quantize (so they can store weights on site). They are interested in Redwood's KV cache and batch controls but require those features to run entirely offline. Asked about runtime kernel signing and a chain of custody for model binaries.

Operational constraints: SCIF access windows limit on‑site work to 2 weeks per quarter; hardware vendor must support delivery into SCIF with sealed manifests. HSM vendor: Thales/Entrust (they will confirm). Current environment: air‑gapped CentOS 8 fleet, orchestration via internal Kubernetes variant, disconnected package repo.

POC plan (high level): prep sealed VM images (Redwood Private), deliver to site, run 2‑week validation with customer datasets (sanitized), demonstrate model swap via signed tarball, hand off STIG hardening docs.

Next asks from ASA: detailed SOW, STIG checklist sample, model update workflow for removable media, estimated committed pricing for a 3‑year Dedicated Private contract. AE note: push to get SecOps architecture review completed (Liam O'Connor to lead with ASA SecOps).
